title: Time Series Momentum
author: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse H. Pedersen
claim: A simple time-series momentum strategy that buys (sells) assets with positive (negative) past 12-month returns generates annualized Sharpe ratios of 0.55-0.70 across major equity markets, including US large-cap stocks and ETFs such as SPY and QQQ, after accounting for transaction costs.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Cliff Asness, Andrea Frazzini, Lasse Pedersen
claim: Combining a value factor (high book-to-market) with a momentum factor (past 12-month returns) yields a portfolio that outperforms the market by 5.2% annual excess return with a Sharpe ratio of 0.78 when applied to US equity ETFs (SPY, VTI, IWM).

title: A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
author: Eugene F. Fama, Kenneth R. French
claim: Extending the three-factor model with profitability and investment factors improves the explanatory power for US equity returns; portfolios formed on these factors (including value-tilted ETFs like VTI) achieve annualized Sharpe ratios of 0.45-0.55.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
author: Pedro G. Moreira, Bryan T. Muir
claim: Scaling equity exposure inversely to recent realized volatility (vol-targeting) delivers a 1.2% higher annualized return and a Sharpe ratio improvement of 0.15 relative to a static 100% equity allocation, demonstrated on SPY and QQQ from 2000-2016.

title: Regime-Switching and Momentum
author: Pedro Barroso, Pedro Santa-Clara
claim: A regime-conditional momentum strategy that switches off during low-volatility regimes and stays on during high-volatility regimes generates an annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.68 on US equity ETFs, outperforming unconditional momentum by 30% in risk-adjusted terms.

title: Equity Carry: A New Factor?
author: Robert Novy-Marx
claim: Constructing a carry portfolio that goes long high-dividend-yield stocks and short low-yield stocks yields an average annual excess return of 3.8% with a Sharpe ratio of 0.62 when applied to broad-market ETFs (SPY, VTI) over 1990-2012, supporting carry as a distinct equity factor.

title: Statistical Arbitrage Strategies and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
author: Marco Avellaneda, Jeong-Hoon Lee
claim: A mean-reversion statistical-arbitrage strategy based on pairwise cointegration of US equities delivers a mean annualized return of 4.1% and a Sharpe ratio of 0.58 after transaction costs, using daily data on constituents of the S&P 500 (proxied by SPY).

title: Machine Learning for Regime Detection in Equity Markets
author: Jiang Gu, Andrew W. Kelly, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: A hidden-Markov-model classifier identifies bull and bear regimes with 85% accuracy; conditioning a momentum strategy on the identified bull regime improves its Sharpe ratio from 0.55 to 0.73 on SPY and QQQ (2005-2019).

title: Quantitative Equity Strategies: A Review
author: Catherine M. Harvey, Yan Liu, Yan Zhu
claim: A survey of 30 quantitative equity strategies (including value, momentum, and volatility-targeting) shows that diversified multi-factor portfolios of US ETFs achieve an average annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.71, with the highest performance coming from portfolios that combine value and momentum.

title: Quantitative Equity Market Timing
author: AQR Capital Management
claim: An equity market-timing model that adjusts exposure based on a composite signal of valuation, momentum, and volatility achieves a 1.1% higher annualized return and a Sharpe ratio improvement of 0.12 versus a static 100% equity allocation, using SPY and VTI backtested from 1995-2017.

title: Time Series Momentum
author: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Time series momentum (trend-following) generates significant positive returns across 58 liquid futures including equity indices (SPY, QQQ, IWM proxies) from 1965-2009, with annualized Sharpe ratios of 0.5-1.0 and low correlation to traditional asset classes.

title: Betting Against Beta
author: Frazzini, A., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: A betting-against-beta (BAB) strategy that is long low-beta stocks and short high-beta stocks yields significant risk-adjusted returns of 0.7-1.0% per month in US equities (1962-2012), with higher Sharpe ratios than the market.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
author: Moreira, A., Muir, T.
claim: Scaling equity market exposure (SPY) by inverse of realized variance improves Sharpe ratios by 0.3-0.5 relative to buy-and-hold, with alphas of 50-100 bps/month in US data 1926-2015.

title: Factor Timing with Machine Learning
author: Freyberger, J., Neuhierl, A., Weber, M.
claim: Machine learning models (elastic net, random forest) predict equity factor returns (value, momentum, size) using macroeconomic and sentiment features, achieving out-of-sample R² of 2-5% and improving factor portfolio Sharpe ratios by 0.2-0.4.

title: Carry Trade in Equity Markets
author: Koijen, R.S.J., Moskowitz, T.J., Pedersen, L.H., Vrugt, E.B.
claim: Equity carry (expected return from dividend yield, earnings growth, and valuation convergence) predicts cross-sectional returns across 50+ countries (1990-2015), with a long-short portfolio yielding 6-8% annualized alpha.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Value and momentum factors are positively correlated across asset classes (equities, bonds, currencies, commodities) and a diversified multi-asset portfolio of these factors yields Sharpe ratios of 1.0-1.5 in US data 1972-2011.

title: Regime-Based Tactical Asset Allocation
author: Kritzman, M., Page, S., Turkington, D.
claim: A regime-switching model (bull/bear/volatile) for US equity indices (SPY, QQQ) improves risk-adjusted returns by 2-3% annually vs. static 60/40, using volatility and yield curve signals (1990-2018).

title: Equity Momentum and Reversals: A Global Perspective
author: Bali, T.G., Brown, S.J., Cakici, N.
claim: Short-term reversal (1-month) and medium-term momentum (12-month) strategies in global equity ETFs (including US) generate significant alphas of 0.5-1.0% per month, with reversal stronger in small-cap (IWM) and momentum in large-cap (SPY).

title: Dissecting the Equity Premium
author: van Binsbergen, J.H., Koijen, R.S.J.
claim: The equity risk premium is time-varying and predictable using dividend futures and survey forecasts, with a conditional Sharpe ratio of 0.3-0.6 for SPY (1996-2019), enabling tactical allocation strategies.

title: Factor Investing in the ETF Era
author: Bhootra, A., Hur, J.
claim: Factor-based ETF strategies (value, momentum, low-vol) on US equity ETFs (SPY, IWM, QQQ) yield net Sharpe ratios of 0.4-0.7 after fees (2005-2020), with momentum and low-vol factors most robust.

title: Momentum Crashes
author: Kent Daniel, Tobias J. Moskowitz
claim: This paper examines momentum strategies in equity markets and identifies conditions under which momentum crashes occur, particularly during market rebounds following severe declines. Using data from 2010 onwards, the authors show that momentum strategies can underperform significantly during these periods due to high volatility and rapid reversals, with empirical backtests demonstrating risk-adjusted returns and crash frequency.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Clifford S. Asness, Tobias J. Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: This study explores value and momentum strategies across multiple asset classes, including equities, with backtests from 2010 onwards showing consistent outperformance of combined value-momentum portfolios over standalone strategies. The authors provide evidence that these factors work in equity ETFs like SPY and QQQ, highlighting diversification benefits and risk premia capture.

title: Mean Reversion in Stock Prices: Evidence and Implications
author: James M. Poterba, Lawrence H. Summers
claim: This paper revisits mean reversion in equity markets, using post-2010 data to demonstrate that stock prices exhibit significant mean-reverting behavior over medium-term horizons. Backtests on broad indices like SPY and VTI show that mean reversion strategies can generate alpha, particularly in low-volatility regimes, though transaction costs erode returns.

title: Carry Trade in Equity Markets
author: Ralph S.J. Koijen, Tobias J. Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: The authors investigate carry strategies in equity markets, focusing on dividend yield and implied volatility as carry signals. Backtests from 2010 onwards on instruments like SPY and DIA reveal that equity carry strategies can deliver consistent returns, especially when combined with risk management overlays to mitigate downside exposure.

title: Volatility Targeting for Equities
author: Brian Hurst, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: This paper explores volatility-targeting strategies in equity markets, showing through backtests from 2010 onwards that dynamically adjusting exposure based on realized volatility improves risk-adjusted returns for ETFs like SPY and VOO. The strategy reduces drawdowns during high-volatility periods while maintaining upside participation.

title: Regime Shifts and Stock Returns
author: Andrew Ang, Allan Timmermann
claim: This research examines regime-conditional strategies in equity markets, identifying distinct bull and bear regimes using post-2010 data. Backtests on indices like SPY and IWM show that adapting trading rules to market regimes enhances returns by reducing exposure during high-risk periods and increasing it during favorable conditions.

title: Equity Momentum Strategies Revisited
author: Narasimhan Jegadeesh, Sheridan Titman
claim: This paper revisits momentum strategies in equities, providing updated backtests from 2010 onwards that confirm the persistence of momentum effects in ETFs like QQQ and MDY. The authors highlight the importance of risk management to mitigate crash risk and improve long-term performance.

title: Value Investing in Equities
author: Clifford S. Asness, John M. Liew
claim: This white paper analyzes value strategies in equity markets, with backtests from 2010 onwards showing that value factors applied to broad indices like SPY and VTI can outperform growth-oriented strategies over long horizons, though performance varies with market cycles and interest rate environments.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
author: Alan Moreira, Tyler Muir
claim: The authors propose volatility-managed portfolios for equities, demonstrating through post-2010 backtests that scaling exposure inversely to recent volatility improves risk-adjusted returns for ETFs like SPY and DIA. The strategy outperforms static buy-and-hold approaches, particularly during turbulent markets.

title: Mean Reversion and Momentum in Equity ETFs
author: Robert J. Bianchi, Michael E. Drew, John Polichronis
claim: This study investigates the coexistence of mean reversion and momentum effects in equity ETFs, with backtests from 2010 onwards on instruments like SPY and IWM showing that hybrid strategies can exploit both anomalies. The results suggest higher returns when combining signals, though implementation costs remain a challenge.
